extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners (IPEA) and practitioners/applicants preparing or responding to PCT international preliminary examination reports and U.S. national stage filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, finalizing, transmitting, and interpreting the International Preliminary Examination Report (PCT Chapter II) and related procedural steps for IPEAs and applicants, including U.S. national stage requirements under 35 U.S.C. 371.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box I — Top‑up searches and supplementary searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. I, item 6 must indicate whether top‑up searches have been carried out by the IPEA; if carried out, the date of the top‑up search and whether additional relevant documents were discovered must be indicated. If a document discovered in the top‑up search is used to support any negative statement with respect to claimed subject matter, it should be cited in Box No. V of the report. Documents that refer to an oral disclosure, use, exhibition or other means that occurred prior to the international filing date and documents that refer to an earlier patent document published on or after the international filing date should be cited in Box VI of the report. Box No. I, item 7 must be marked if the report is established taking into account the supplementary international search report(s) from the specified SISA(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate dates and whether additional relevant documents were found; cite top‑up search documents in Box V if relied on for negative findings; distinguish documents to be reported in Box VI (non‑written disclosures or later publications of earlier filings). Mark use of SISA reports in the supplemental item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box II — Priority treated as not made; grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. II informs the applicant that the report is established as if the priority claim had not been made. This may occur when: (A) the IPEA requested but was not furnished a copy of the earlier application whose priority is claimed (PCT Rule 66.7(a)); (B) applicant failed to timely comply with an invitation to furnish a translation of the earlier application (PCT Rule 66.7(b)); (C) the priority claim is found invalid or all claims are directed to inventions not described and enabled by the earlier application (PCT Rule 64.1); (D) the description, claims or drawings are so unclear that no meaningful opinion could be formed; (E) the claims are so inadequately supported by the description that no meaningful opinion could be formed; (F) no international search report has been established for the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which claims are affected if the report is not established only as to certain claims. Indicate withdrawal of the priority claim where applicable. Provide explicit reasons for treating the application as if priority not claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing non‑compliance reason
rubrics_metrics.description: If a meaningful opinion could not be formed because the nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence listing does not comply with WIPO Standard ST.26 and/or the applicant did not pay the late furnishing fee, the examiner must indicate the reason for non‑compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether failure is due to ST.26 non‑compliance or unpaid late furnishing fee and link this to inability to form a meaningful opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box III — Non‑establishment of opinion on novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability
rubrics_metrics.description: Box No. III indicates that the report has not been established on questions of novelty, inventive step or industrial applicability as to some or all claims. The examiner must specify that the report was not established because, for example: (A) the application relates to subject matter which does not require international preliminary examination; (D) the applicant has neither restricted the claims nor paid additional fees; (E) the examiner considered the international application did not comply with unity of invention but decided not to issue an invitation to restrict or pay additional fees. Where less than all claims are examined, the examiner must indicate which parts were and which parts were not the subject of international preliminary examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give precise reasons for non‑establishment and identify the exact claims or parts not examined. Use the enumerated grounds from PCT Rules and internal guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box IV — Lack of unity of invention and handling of additional fees/restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant has paid additional fees or restricted claims in response to an invitation, or failed to respond, the IPR report shall indicate whether: (A) the claims have been restricted; (B) additional fees have been paid without protest; (C) additional fees have been paid by the applicant under protest; (D) the applicant has neither restricted nor paid additional fees. If additional fees were paid under protest and the applicant requested it, the text of the protest and the decision thereon must be annexed to the report by IPEA personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State clearly whether restriction occurred or fees were paid and whether payments were protested; attach protest text and decision where requested by applicant; if indication under item (E) (examiner thought unity lacking but did not issue invitation), specify reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box V — Reasoned statement on novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability (Article 35(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner must indicate whether each claim appears to satisfy novelty, inventive step (nonobviousness), and industrial applicability. Determinations should be made for each criterion separately and should be negative if the criterion is not satisfied for that claim. The examiner should always cite documents believed to support any negative determination as to novelty and inventive step. Any negative holding on industrial applicability must be fully explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explanations referencing the cited documents and identify relevant passages (page/column/lines). Preferably provide a reasoned statement in all instances. Follow document citation procedure per Administrative Instructions Sections 503 and 611. If a statement is positive and the reason for citing a document is obvious, less explanation may suffice; otherwise give detailed rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VI — Identification of certain cited documents (non‑written disclosures and later publications)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner or the international search report cites a relevant document referring to a non‑written disclosure and the document was published on or after the relevant date, the examiner must indicate: (A) the date the document was made available to the public; and (B) the date the non‑written public disclosure occurred. The examiner should also identify any published application or patent which would constitute prior art for purposes of PCT Article 33(2) and (3) had it been published earlier but was filed prior to, or claims the priority of, an earlier application filed prior to the relevant date. For each such published application or patent provide publication date, filing date, and claimed priority date (if any). The report may also indicate that the priority date of the document cited has not been validly claimed (PCT Rule 70.10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the dates precisely and follow Administrative Instructions Sections 507(c)–(e) and 508 for indicating special categories of documents and the claims to which the documents are relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VII — Opinion on defects in form or contents
rubrics_metrics.description: If defects in the form or contents of the international application have not been suitably solved by the time limit for establishing the report, the examiner may include this opinion in the report and must indicate the reasons for the opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the specific defects remaining and the reasons why they are not suitably solved; see MPEP §1845.01 for further discussion. Ensure annexes, if any, accompany the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Box VIII — Observations on clarity and support
rubrics_metrics.description: If, in the examiner's opinion, clarity of the claims, description, drawings, or the question of whether the claims are fully supported by the description have not been suitably solved at the prescribed time limit, the examiner may include this observation in the report and must indicate the reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete examples of lack of clarity or insufficient support and refer to the relevant parts of the application; see MPEP §1845.01 for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalization — Authorized officer, signatures, and sheet counts
rubrics_metrics.description: The name of the authorized officer responsible for the report must be indicated. An 'authorized officer' is the person who actually performed the examination work or supervised it; the file copy of the report must be signed by a primary examiner. The total number of sheets of the international preliminary examination report, including the cover sheet, must be indicated. For annexes to be sent to the applicant and to the International Bureau, indicate total sheets of amended description, claims and/or drawings, sheets containing rectifications authorized by the IPEA, superseded or cancelled sheets, and any accompanying letters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure an authorized officer is named (need not have signatory authority) and primary examiner signs the file copy. Accurately count and report all sheets and note any superseded or rectified sheets per PCT Rules and Administrative Instructions (e.g., Rules 46.5, 66.8, 70.16, 91.2; Admin Instr. Sec. 607).

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexes — Electronic carriers and sequence listing indications
rubrics_metrics.description: For annexes sent to the International Bureau only, indicate the type and number of electronic carrier(s) containing a sequence listing (in electronic form only) as indicated in the Supplemental Box Relating to Sequence Listing (see paragraph 3 bis of Annex C of the PCT Administrative Instructions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record carrier types/quantities in the Supplemental Box and ensure conformity with rules for sequence listings and electronic submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start conditions for international preliminary examination (PCT Rule 69.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The IPEA shall start international preliminary examination when it is in possession of: (i) the demand; (ii) the amount due in full for the handling fee and preliminary examination fee (including late payment fee where applicable); and (iii) either the international search report or the declaration that no search report will be established and the written opinion under Rule 43bis.1. Additional rules govern postponement if amendments are indicated or not furnished and if applicant requests postponement under Rule 54bis.1(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not start examination until required documents/fees are received. If the ISA and IPEA are the same office and they wish to start at same time, additional conditions apply (see paragraphs (b) and (b‑bis)). Respect instructions about amendments under Article 19 or 34 and invitations under Rule 60.1(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishing the international preliminary examination report (PCT Rule 69.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for establishing the report is whichever of the following periods expires last: (i) 28 months from the priority date; or (ii) six months from the time provided under Rule 69.1 for the start of the international preliminary examination; or (iii) six months from the date of receipt by the IPEA of the translation furnished under Rule 55.2. Internally the Office may use a 27‑month internal deadline to ensure sufficient processing time so the report reaches the International Bureau by 28 months from the earliest priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute and observe the correct latest‑expiring period. Account for postponement requests under Rule 54bis.1(a) and for the timing consequences of indicated or missing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of report and annexes (PCT Article 36; Rule 71)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international preliminary examination report together with prescribed annexes shall be transmitted to the applicant and to the International Bureau. The IPEA shall, on the same day, transmit one copy of the report and annexes to the International Bureau and one copy to the applicant. The transmittal is effected using Notification of Preliminary Report on Patentability (Form PCT/IPEA/416). The name of the authorized officer responsible for the international preliminary report must be indicated on Form PCT/IPEA/416.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmit copies promptly and make every effort to reach the IB before expiration of the PCT Rule 69.2 time limit. Ensure Form PCT/IPEA/416 is fully completed with authorized officer details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited documents — availability, time limits, and costs (PCT Rule 71.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for copies of cited documents under Article 36(4) may be presented any time during seven years from the international filing date. The IPEA may require the requesting party (applicant or elected Office) to pay the cost of preparing and mailing the copies; the level of cost will be provided for in agreements between IPEAs and the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inform requestors of possible charges and availability period; IPEAs may delegate performance of obligations to another agency responsible to them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations — language of report and annexes (PCT Rules 70.17, 72)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report and any annex shall be in the language in which the international application is published, or, if the IPE is carried out on the basis of a translation, in the language of that translation. Any elected State may require the report (if not in an official language of its national Office) be translated into English; such requirements are to be notified to the International Bureau. The International Bureau prepares translations of the body of the report or written opinion; translations of annexes are the applicant's responsibility. The U.S. requires the final report and annexes to be in English; translations of annexes for national stage purposes are required under 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(5) and 37 CFR 1.495(e); failure to timely provide such translations results in cancellation of the annexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing or receiving reports, confirm required languages and who bears responsibility for translations. Applicants should timely furnish annex translations for national stage compliance where required (e.g., U.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality of the international preliminary examination (PCT Article 38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless requested or authorized by the applicant, neither the International Bureau nor the IPEA shall allow access to the file of the international preliminary examination prior to establishment of the report, except that elected Offices may access the file once the report has been established. Subject to these provisions, the IB and IPEA shall not give information on issuance/non‑issuance of the report or on withdrawal/non‑withdrawal of the demand or elections, unless requested/authorized by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect applicant confidentiality requests. After establishment of the report, access and communications are governed by Articles 36 and 37 and PCT Rules 94.2/94.3; U.S. CFR provisions (37 CFR 1.11, 1.14, etc.) set additional conditions for access and copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of demand or elections (PCT Article 37; Rule 90bis; Admin Instr. Sec. 606)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw any or all elections at any time prior to expiration of 30 months from the priority date; if all elected States' elections are withdrawn, the demand is considered withdrawn. Withdrawal is effective upon receipt of a notice addressed to the International Bureau. Withdrawals must be signed by all applicants in accordance with PCT Rule 90bis.5; the IPEA shall cancel ex officio elections of any State not a designated State or not bound by Chapter II, marking the cancellation and notifying the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transmit withdrawal notices promptly to the IB and elected Offices; if filing withdrawal with the IPEA, the IPEA must mark the date and promptly transmit it to the IB. Observe signature and power‑of‑attorney requirements; do not waive separate POA requirements in withdrawals.

rubrics_metrics.name: National stage (U.S. 35 U.S.C. 371) — identification and required submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: When entering the U.S. national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, once a U.S. application number is accorded, that number should be used in communications; include international application number, international filing date, and national stage entry date for cross‑checking. The national stage commences upon expiration of applicable time limits under Articles 22 or 39. The applicant shall file in the USPTO: (1) the national fee (section 41(a)); (2) a copy of the international application and an English translation if filed in another language (unless already communicated by the IB); (3) amendments to claims made under Article 19 (unless already communicated) and translations if made in another language; (4) an oath or declaration complying with section 115; and (5) an English translation of any annexes to the international preliminary examination report if the annexes were made in another language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the U.S. application number for speedier processing. Ensure required fees, translations, and declarations are timely filed to avoid issues. Understand that the national stage differs from domestic filings in timing and that the prior art status is usually better known at national stage.
